# cachyos-pro — custom GRUB theme. Assets are generated by build-assets.sh, do not hand-edit them.
# Palette: base #0A0E17..#121A2B · accent #07B9C7 (CachyOS brand, sampled from the stock theme) · text #D6DEEA
# Layout: one centred axis at x=960 (title, menu, countdown) — the menu box is 580..1340 and the
# highlight sits 16 px inside it on both sides (item_padding), which is why the bar is 596..1324.
#
# Gotchas learned the hard way (keep these true if you edit):
#   * styled-box PNGs must carry their transparency in an alpha channel (write them with
#     ImageMagick's PNG32:). GRUB does decode palette PNGs, but it ignores the tRNS chunk, so a
#     palette+alpha slice renders fully OPAQUE; grayscale and interlaced PNGs are rejected outright.
#   * font names come from grub-mkfont WITHOUT -n; with -n GRUB sees "<family> Regular <size>", the
#     lookup misses and it silently renders in whichever font happened to load first.
#   * a missing desktop-image is FATAL (theme load aborts -> plain text menu); a missing box slice
#     is silent; a typo in a *global* property aborts the theme while a typo in a component
#     property is silently ignored.

title-text: ""
desktop-image: "background.png"
desktop-image-scale-method: "stretch"
desktop-color: "#0A0E17"

# 'c' shell: GRUB renders this on its own plain console (the theme's terminal-box is not
# honoured there), so only the monospace font is set — no dead box declaration.
terminal-font: "Terminus Regular 18"

# title — centred on the same axis as the menu (x = 620..1300)
+ label {
  left = 580
  top = 84
  width = 760
  height = 56
  align = "center"
  text = "CachyOS"
  font = "Cantarell Bold 48"
  color = "#FFFFFF"
}

# boot menu — height must exceed items*item_height + spacing*(items-1) or the last entry is not drawn.
# item_spacing ≈ 0.25-0.30 × item_height is the norm across surveyed themes (vinceliuice, matter,
# starfield, catppuccin); 4 px was tighter than every one of them.
# The whole block is centred: left = (1920 - 760) / 2 = 580. A left-docked menu leaves a dead right
# half that no amount of background motif fixes, and centring also removes the title-vs-entry axis
# mismatch.
# width 760 = the old 710 of label room + a 40 px icon + its 20 px gutter, with the labels measured
# from the real generated menu: with GRUB_BTRFS_TITLE_FORMAT = ("date" "snapshot" "type") the longest
# snapshot submenu title is 642 px and the kernel rows are 640 px, so 760 still leaves 668 px of text
# room (~26 px headroom). The default format includes the free-text description and reaches 1438 px,
# which would not fit at any width this menu can use.
+ boot_menu {
  left = 580
  top = 200
  width = 760
  height = 400
  item_font = "Cantarell Regular 24"
  selected_item_font = "inherit"
  item_color = "#C3CCDB"
  selected_item_color = "#FFFFFF"
  item_height = 56
  item_padding = 16
  item_spacing = 16
  icon_width = 40
  icon_height = 40
  item_icon_space = 20
  selected_item_pixmap_style = "select_*.png"
}

# countdown, grouped directly under the menu so the countdown and the choice it will make are
# in one visual cluster (it used to sit at the bottom edge, 330 px away from the menu).
# x/width match the SELECTED ROW's visible extent, not the menu box: GRUB insets the highlight by
# item_padding, so the highlight measures 596..1324 while the box is 580..1340 — a bar on the box
# sticks out ~16 px past the highlight on each side (measured on the render).
+ progress_bar {
  id = "__timeout__"
  left = 596
  top = 600
  width = 728
  height = 4
  fg_color = "#07B9C7"
  bg_color = "#243046"
}

# countdown text (same extent as the bar, so both stay centred on the menu axis at x=960)
+ label {
  id = "__timeout__"
  left = 596
  top = 618
  width = 728
  height = 26
  align = "center"
  text = "Starting in %d seconds"
  font = "Cantarell Regular 19"
  color = "#AEB9C9"
}

# key hints — GRUB fills this in, localised; centred along the bottom edge
+ label {
  left = 0
  top = 1008
  width = 1920
  height = 22
  align = "center"
  text = "@KEYMAP_MIDDLE@"
  font = "Cantarell Regular 19"
  color = "#9AA6B8"
}
